item.text:
**Assessment**
Mostly no. Sisi’s 2024 response to flare-ups mixed a few restraint signals on Gaza/border spillover and some limited detention reform with a much larger pattern of arrests, incommunicado detention, and coercive control of protest and refugee flows. The strongest positive evidence is external crisis mediation and defensive border posture, not a broadly protection-oriented domestic response.

- **Egypt, U.S. and Qatar urge immediate Gaza ceasefire and bridging proposal** | Presidency of the Republic of Egypt | August 8, 2024 | [link](https://www.presidency.eg/EN/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news882024-3/)  
  The joint statement called for immediate relief, a ceasefire, and a bridging proposal to close remaining gaps. This is strong restraint/de-escalation evidence in a major regional crisis, though it is not a domestic public-order response.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- **Egypt raises preparedness level in northern Sinai, security sources say** | Reuters via MarketScreener | May 6, 2024 | [link](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Egypt-raises-preparedness-level-in-northern-Sinai-security-sources-say-46636165/)  
  Egypt raised military preparedness in northern Sinai after the Rafah operation began. This is the clearest narrow-defensive response to a spillover risk, and it is more restrained than an escalatory move.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.10`

- **Egypt’s Sisi, Blinken discuss ways to move forward in Gaza ceasefire negotiations** | Reuters via ThePrint | August 20, 2024 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/egypts-sisi-blinken-discuss-ways-to-move-forward-in-gaza-ceasefire-negotiations/2230632/)  
  Sisi warned about regional expansion of the Gaza war and framed a ceasefire as the basis of regional stability. This supports a de-escalatory crisis-management reading rather than a militarized or incendiary one.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- **Egypt pardons prisoners on Police Day and January 25 Revolution** | Human Rights Studies - Egypt / SIS | January 25, 2024 | [link](https://hrightsstudies.sis.gov.eg/en/press/local/egypt-pardons-prisoners-on-Police-Day-and-January-25-Revolution/)  
  Sisi signed a pardon for eligible prisoners, including some convicted for political expression and political activity. This is a limited positive signal for restraint after domestic tension, but it is episodic clemency rather than a durable crisis-response model.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.6`, `3B.4`

- **Sisi orders government to act on National Dialogue recommendations** | Presidency of the Republic of Egypt | August 21, 2024 | [link](https://www.presidency.eg/fr/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news2182024/)  
  The presidency said Sisi instructed the government to shorten pretrial detention and activate alternatives to detention. This is the strongest official due-process reform signal in 2024, but it does not outweigh the broader coercive response to protests and civic mobilization.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.6`, `3B.4`

- **Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests** | Amnesty International | July 18, 2024 | [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/)  
  Security forces detained 119 people after protest calls over prices and power cuts, using incommunicado detention, blindfolding, and broad security charges. That is direct evidence of a fear response built around suppression and selective punishment, not protection.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`

- **Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis** | Amnesty International | May 13, 2024 | [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/)  
  Amnesty documented arrests of protesters, striking workers, and online critics, plus dispersal of protests and beatings/electroshock without proper investigation. This is strong evidence that domestic crisis management relied on retaliation and intimidation.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`

- **Egypt: Release protesters and activists detained over Palestine solidarity** | Amnesty International | June 14, 2024 | [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-release-protesters-and-activists-detained-over-palestine-solidarity/)  
  More than 123 people were arrested for peaceful Palestine solidarity or criticism of the Rafah closure, with reports of incommunicado detention and ill-treatment. This is evidence of selective punishment in response to spontaneous civic flare-ups.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.6`, `3B.5`

- **Egypt: “Handcuffed like dangerous criminals”: Arbitrary detention and forced returns of Sudanese refugees in Egypt** | Amnesty International | June 19, 2024 | [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/mde12/8101/2024/en/)  
  Border police and Border Guard Forces mass-arrested Sudanese refugees, held women, men, and children in cruel conditions, and forcibly returned them without asylum access. This is collective punitive control, not protection or restraint.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `3B.7`, `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`

- **President El-Sisi Inaugurates Egypt International Airshow (EIAS) 2024** | State Information Service | September 3, 2024 | [link](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/events/president-el-sisi-inaugurates-egypt-international-airshow-eias-2024/)  
  Egypt staged a major defense-industrial airshow with military hardware, prestige messaging, and broad foreign participation. This is not a crisis response itself, but it undercuts any clean claim that 2024 responses were centered on civilian restraint rather than militarized spectacle.  
  QIDs: `3B.9`, `2B.10`, `2B.4`

**Search gap**
I did not find evidence that Sisi developed a consistent, civilian-protection-focused domestic crisis protocol in 2024. The positive material is mostly about Gaza mediation, Sinai spillover defense, and small detention reforms. The domestic record still tilts heavily toward arrest, censorship, and coercive control when protests or economic flare-ups emerged.
